title: United in Diversity? Contextual Biases in LLM-Based Predictions of the 2024 European Parliament Elections
abstract: arXiv:2409.09045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: "Silicon samples" based on large language models (LLMs) have been argued to serve as efficient alternatives to surveys of humans, assuming that their training data includes information on human attitudes and behavior. However, LLM-generated survey data might exhibit biases, for example due to a lack of diversity in training and alignment processes, which risk reinforcing existing biases in research and policymaking. Before the elections have taken place, we prompt three LLMs with individual-level background information of 26,000 eligible European voters to predict each person's voting behavior. translated_title: 团结于多样性之中？基于大语言模型的2024年欧洲议会选举预测中的情境偏差
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的“硅基样本”被认为是人类调查的高效替代方案，其前提是模型的训练数据中包含有关人类态度和行为的信息。然而，LLM生成的调查数据可能存在偏差，例如由于训练和对齐过程中缺乏多样性，这有加剧研究与政策制定中既有偏差的风险。在本研究中，我们通过预测2024年欧盟选举的结果，考察基于LLM的个人公众舆论预测在多大程度上表现出情境依赖性偏差。在选举举行之前，我们向三个大语言模型提供26,000名具备投票资格的欧洲选民的个体层面背景信息，以预测每个人的投票行为。我们研究表明，与实际选举结果相比，基于LLM的未来投票行为预测在很大程度上是失败的，且其准确性在不同情境之间分布不均。
tldr: 本研究在2024年欧洲议会选举前利用三个大语言模型基于26,000名欧洲选民的个体背景信息预测其投票行为，发现LLM预测与实际结果相比大多失败且准确性在不同情境间分布不均，揭示了LLM舆论预测中存在的情境依赖性偏差。
en_tdlr: By prompting three LLMs with individual-level background information of 26,000 eligible European voters to predict voting behavior in the 2024 European Parliament elections, this study shows that LLM-based predictions largely fail against actual results and their accuracy is unequally distributed across contexts, revealing context-dependent biases in LLM-based public opinion prediction.
